title: WaitForChild()
summary: Yields until a child with the given name exists (or a timeout passes). The standard cure for 'replication hasn't arrived yet' nil errors, especially on the client.

parameters.name: childName
parameters.description: Name of the child to wait for.

parameters.name: timeLimit
parameters.description: Max seconds to wait. Without it, waits forever (and warns after ~5s). With it, returns nil on timeout.

reference.returns: The child instance — or nil if the time limit expired.

details.heading: Yields
details.body: If the child isn't there yet, the calling thread pauses until it appears. Instant return when it already exists.

explanation.whatItIs: 'Hold the line until it shows up.' Clients start running scripts before every replicated object arrives; WaitForChild bridges that gap.
explanation.whyItExists: Replication is asynchronous — the number one source of 'attempt to index nil' on clients is reaching for content that's still in transit.
whenToUse: Client startup: remotes, modules, GUI templates in ReplicatedStorage
Waiting on character parts right after CharacterAdded (edge cases)
Any child that SHOULD exist but might not exist YET
whenNotToUse: When absence is a normal outcome — FindFirstChild + nil check instead
In RenderStepped or tight loops (it yields)
With no timeout on optional content — a misspelled name hangs forever (you'll get warnings after ~5s)
tips: Client rule of thumb: WaitForChild for replicated content; FindFirstChild for may-not-exist content
Always check the nil result when using a timeout
commonMistakes: WaitForChild("MispelledName") with no timeout → script hangs silently
Using it server-side for content the server already owns — unnecessary
Calling it every frame — wait ONCE at startup and cache the reference

examples.title: Safe client startup
examples.code:
-- LocalScript
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local remotes = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Remotes", 10)
if not remotes then
    error("Remotes folder never replicated — check server setup")
end

local buyEvent = remotes:WaitForChild("Buy", 5)
if buyEvent then
    print("Ready to shop")
end
examples.whyItWorks: Timeouts convert 'hang forever' into 'nil you can handle' — and the error message tells you exactly what's missing.
